headline: RUNTIME: a full replay is already fast, so speed is not the case for an event table. Warm replay of one month: 0.13-0.47 s (shipped preset), 0.01-0.08 s (calibrated). Nine one-month runs sum to 2.20 s warm / 6.0 s cold (shipped) and 0.31 s / 3.8 s (calibrated), plus 8 s feed loading and a one-time numba compile of 34.3 s (empty cache; 0.13-0.17 s when loaded from cache). The project's own queue logs agree: 0.34 s per replay in the calibrated one-at-a-time sweep (329 in 113 s), 1.7-2.0 s in shipped-preset sweeps, about 5 s when the FlashGold micro series changes. Reason: the engine skips idle ticks and visits only 36.6% (22.97M of 62.73M) of ticks for the shipped preset and 3.3% (2.06M) for the calibrated one, not 60 million.

MEMORY: peak RSS 0.59-0.95 GB for one month (2026-03, 9.2M ticks, is the largest at 0.95 GB; the peak is the feed load; 1.35 GB in the process that also compiled numba), so 2026-03 was run, the 4 GB limit was never near. Full feed extrapolates to about 6.5-7 GB (not run).

EVENT VOLUMES, 9 months (sum of nine one-month runs; the project's continuous run has 20,688,003 decisions, match within 0.02%): shipped preset 20.69M direction evaluations (C_DECISIONS; Oct 1.37M, Mar 4.26M), 2.31M engine alerts, 12.55M alert-candidate ticks at x7.5 (20.0% of ticks) in 127,418 episodes (20 s merge; 311k at a 5 s merge, 43k at 60 s), 23.5k orders, 9.2k fills; 81% of decisions end with no winning side, 8% at the spread cap, 7% at the FlashGold gate. Calibrated preset (x30, cap 14): 1.80M decisions, 39k alerts, 330,585 candidate ticks (0.53%) in 17,845 episodes, 2,643 orders, 1,236 fills; 75% of its decisions die at the spread cap, 24% have no winner, 1.4% reach the FlashGold gate.

EVENT TABLE SIZE AND SPEED (prototype built and timed on 2026-03 and 2026-10): one row per decision = 136 B (tick index + 21 decision features + 11 forward outcomes: mid move at 1/2/5/10/20/30/60 s and max up/down within 30/60 s) = 2.81 GB for 20.7M shipped-style rows, 245 MB for 1.8M calibrated-style rows (about 65 B/row estimated with int16 columns: 1.35 GB / 0.12 GB). Build 7.5 s per 4.26M-row month (2.3 GB peak), about 30-36 s for nine months single-threaded. Re-scoring one candidate direction rule: numba 11 ms per 4.26M rows (55-75 ms for nine months) vs numpy 0.40 s (about 2 s) against 2.2 s for a full shipped-style replay; calibrated-style table 3.5-7 ms numba / 0.08-0.11 s numpy against 0.31 s. So the table pays only with compiled scoring and only for large searches.

TABLE FIDELITY: re-scoring from the logged features reproduced the engine's winner in 99.77-99.97% of rows; every mismatch (0 exceptions) is an exact-threshold tie (spread == cap, |body| == 21, micro distance == 3) decided by float64 noise in the engine; 6.0% (Mar 2026) and 6.5% (Oct 2026) of the calibrated preset's decision rows sit exactly at the 14-point cap, and 64% (Mar) and 46% (Oct) of those fail the engine's float test (Nov 2026: 9.2% and 39%). Episodes are very unequal (median 36-55 rows, p99 1,248-3,743, max 151,484 rows in one March episode); 1 s thinning keeps only 10-20% of rows.

DIRECTION STRUCTURE: in the replay (no order flow) the winning side equals the burst direction in 100% of decisions that have a winner (checked on 0.45M winner rows, Oct and Mar, both presets), so direction means continue the burst or skip; only the EXHL fade (shipped router mode 2, about 5% of decisions) trades against it. Only the flow votes (up to +3.0) can make the score pick the other side or the market route FOLM, which carried 74% of the real trades and which the replay never takes.

SHIPPED PRESET BASELINE (9,282 trades): PF 0.72, win 36.0%, -17.9 pts/trade (calibration 0.69 / validation 0.72 / hold-out 0.83). MFE reached 10/30/60/100 pts in 68.9/59.8/49.7/37.4% of trades, but a driftless path with the same 90-pt stop and 17-pt spread gives 72.3/60.5/48.7/38.7%, so the shares show no skill (excess -3.7/-0.8/+0.8/-1.4). Mid-to-mid move before costs +0.7 +/- 1.2 pts (t 0.6; about 0 in every split, month, side); costs of 18.6 pts vs the quote (half-spreads 17.3) are the whole loss (order-price convention: spread 17.3 + entry slip 3.4 + stop slip 11.8 = 32.5 against gross 14.7).

CALIBRATED PRESET BASELINE (1,234 trades): PF 1.15, win 33.1%, +10.0 pts/trade; gross mid-to-mid +28.3 +/- 5.8 pts before costs (t 4.9; 35.1/22.9/29.8 in calibration/validation/hold-out). Costs per trade: 18.5 vs the quote (spread 16.9, net slippage 1.6) or 51.5 in the order-price convention (spread 16.9 + entry slip 17.5 + stop slip 17.0; 86% of trades end at a stop). Skill is concentrated in buys (+44.5, t 4.8; sells +17.7 but net -2.5), bursts of 150-400 and >=600 pts, spread <=13 at order, and 4 of 9 months; costs differ by 2x between splits (61.8 / 54.1 / 27.7), which is why the hold-out looks best.

REAL ACCOUNT (2,584 trades, 7 Sep-8 Oct 2026): PF 0.83, win 36.2%, -8.5 pts/trade. The flow label does not separate outcomes (agrees 1,609: PF 0.80; disagrees 409: 0.92; none 566: 0.85; disagrees minus agrees +5.7 pts, 95% range about -5.3 to +16.7 (it moves with the seed); the sign flips between BM and SM). Re-managing the 1,621 real entries in the engine gives MFE excess over no-skill of only +1.4/+1.5/+1.8/+0.2 pts for FOLM market entries (z about 1). No hour or session effect in any data set (rank correlation of hourly means between splits -0.3..+0.3).

STATISTICAL POWER: a calibrated trade has SD about 200 pts (SE of the mean 5.8 for 1,236 trades), so two candidates 10 pts apart need about 6,300 trades per arm (25,000 for 5 pts). Nine months hold 1,236 calibrated trades but 17.8k x30 alert episodes and 127k x7.5 episodes, so ranking on fixed-horizon forward moves per episode has 10-100x the samples of ranking on trades.

nine_month_estimate: 9 months = nine one-month runs (a continuous nine-month run needs about 7 GB and was not made; the project's own continuous shipped-preset run has 20,688,003 decisions and 2,308,197 alerts against my 20,692,867 and 2,309,118). Shipped preset: 62.73M ticks, 20.69M decisions, 2.31M alerts, 12.55M candidate ticks (x7.5), 127,418 episodes (20 s merge), 22.97M ticks visited (36.6%), replay 6.0 s cold / 2.20 s warm (+8.3 s feed load, +34.3 s one-time compile, 0.15 s from cache). Calibrated preset: 1.80M decisions, 39,087 alerts, 330,585 candidate ticks (x30), 17,845 episodes, 2.06M ticks visited (3.3%), 3.8 s cold / 0.31 s warm. Decision-event table (one row per C_DECISIONS evaluation, prototype layout 136 B/row): shipped-style 20.69M rows = 2.81 GB (about 1.35 GB at an estimated 65 B/row with int16 columns; 3.3-4.1M rows = 0.45-0.56 GB after 1 s thinning), calibrated-style 1.80M rows = 245 MB (about 117 MB compact; 0.19-0.23M rows after 1 s thinning). Build time 29-36 s single-threaded for the shipped-style table (month by month, 2.3 GB peak for March) and 3.5-5.4 s for the calibrated-style one. Evaluating one candidate over the whole table: 55-75 ms (numba) / about 2 s (numpy) shipped-style; 3.5-7 ms (numba) / 0.08-0.11 s (numpy) calibrated-style; the numba-vs-engine gain is about 30-90x, numpy gives none at shipped-style volume. Candidate-level units: 12.55M candidate ticks (x7.5) or 0.33M (x30); episodes 127k or 17.8k; orders 23.5k or 2.6k; fills 9.2k or 1.2k.

baselines.notes: Sources: replay-ref = results/trades_reference_preset.csv (shipped NativeReference preset, 9,282 trades, 9 months, real-fill execution model); replay-cal = results/center_final_center_trades.csv (calibrated preset, 1,234 trades); real = results/real/real_trades_sar.csv (2,584 real trades, 7 Sep-8 Oct 2026, broker server time, UTC = server - 3 h as in tools/real_replay.py); real-entries-replay = results/real/real_replay_baseline_trades.csv (1,621 real entries re-managed by the engine); cost-cal / cost-ref / fg-gate = my rerun of the engine with extra logging (trades and counters identical to the repository engine in all 18 month runs; adds fill and exit spread, stop level in force, mid at fill and exit; nine one-month runs give 1,236 / 9,241 trades vs 1,234 / 9,282 in the CSVs because the filter and week state restart each month). Metrics: n = closed trades; win_pct = share with pts > 0; pf = sum of winning pts / abs(sum of losing pts); avg_points = mean pts, pts = side x (exit fill - entry fill)/0.01 per 0.01 lot after spread and slippage, commission 0 (1 point = $0.01); t = mean/(sd/sqrt(n)). Splits by entry time: calibration 2025-11-01..2026-02-28, validation 2026-03-01..2026-05-31, hold-out Oct-Nov 2026 (June-Sep 2026 is missing; the calibrated preset was chosen with all three in view). Slices: alert size = abs(mid move) in points over the 10 s lookback at alert start; spread = points at order placement; hour = UTC entry hour (sessions 00-06, 07-11, 12-16, 17-20, 21-23).

MFE (replays only; the real CSV has none) = highest favourable excursion in points between fill and exit on the exit-side quote (bid for longs, ask for shorts) against the entry fill, so it is net of the spread paid on entry, floored at 0 and cut at the exit (stop, target, defensive or speed exit): a lower bound on how far price went the trade's way. mfe_ge_30_pct = share of trades with MFE >= 30 points (10/60/100 shares are in the notes as MFE>=10/60/100). Because a 90-point stop makes small MFE levels easy to reach, notes give MFE30 excess = observed minus a no-skill reference in percentage points; reference for a driftless path: P(MFE >= x before the stop) = D/(D + x + s), s = spread at the fill, D = 90 + entry slippage - s, averaged over the trades (other exits only lower MFE, so it is an upper bound for no skill). gross = mean of side x (mid at exit tick - mid at fill tick)/0.01 before any spread or slippage, with t = mean/SE; for a driftless mid price this averages 0 for any entry and exit rule, so a gross mean away from 0 is direction skill; net = gross - entry cost - exit cost (identity checked on every trade).

Cost vs the quote: entry cost = side x (entry fill - mid at fill tick); exit cost = side x (mid at exit tick - exit fill); both in points (half-spread plus slippage against the quote; snapped fills make the slippage part negative). Order-price convention of REPORT.md: spread = (spread at fill + spread at exit)/2; entry slip = side x (fill - order price)/0.01 (> 0 worse; limit fills with price improvement < 0); stop slip = side x (stop level - exit fill)/0.01 on stop exits (original stop and trailing layer), else 0; gross before costs on that convention = net + the three. The two conventions differ because a stop order that gaps through its price is charged slippage against the order price, but only the half-spread against the quote.

where_direction_skill_exists: GENUINE EDGE BEFORE COSTS exists only in the calibrated regime (alert of at least 30 spreads, spread cap 14, stop entries): gross mid-to-mid +28.3 pts/trade (SE 5.8, t 4.9; +35.1/+22.9/+29.8 in calibration/validation/hold-out, t 3.3/2.8/2.4) against 18.5 pts of cost vs the quote (51.5 in the order-price convention), net +9.8. It is concentrated in: buys (+44.5, t 4.8; sells +17.7, t 2.4, but net -2.5 because sells cost 20.2 vs 15.8); FLXQ:BS +44.2 (t 3.8) and QUAL:BS/SS +45.0/+33.7 (t 2.9/2.6) but not FLXQ:SS (+7.3, t 0.9; -1.6 and -1.0 in validation and hold-out); bursts of 150-400 pts (+30..+38, t 2.0-3.5) and >=600 pts (+81, t 3.0, n 93) but not 400-600 (+9) or 100-150 (-33); spread <=13 at order (+31..+36, t 1.8-3.4) vs 14-16 (+12.5, t 1.3); and four months (Jan, Feb, Mar, Nov 2026: +37..+50, t 2.0-2.8) while the other five are about 0 (-0.3..+11). The FlashGold gate adds direction information in this regime: trades the gate keeps average +31.3 gross (t 5.2), trades taken only without it +7.0 (t 1.0), difference 24.3 +/- 9.2. NO SKILL in: the shipped preset overall (gross +0.7 +/- 1.2, t 0.6; MFE excess -3.7/-0.8/+0.8/-1.4 pts at 10/30/60/100 against a no-skill reference; zero in every split, side and month; its only exception is alerts >=600 pts: n 219, gross +34.8, t 3.2); its EXHL limit fades (-1.2 / -5.2, t -0.4 / -2.0; the market keeps going against them); its FlashGold gate (gross +0.7 on vs +0.1 off); the real account's flow label (disagrees minus agrees +5.7 pts, CI -5.4..+16.7; FOLM re-managed MFE excess +1.4/+1.5/+1.8/+0.2); hour of day or session (rank correlation of hourly mean points between splits -0.3..+0.3 in both replays). Caveats: the calibrated preset was chosen with all three splits in view; costs swing 3x by month (stop-loss slip mean 7-9 pts Oct-Nov 2026 vs 22-37 pts Jan-Mar 2026) and the cost model was fitted on one month of real fills; the replay cannot take the flow-driven market route that made 74% of the real trades; real trades carry no MFE; June-Sep 2026 is missing.
design_implications: Do not justify the event table by replay speed: a 9-month engine replay is 0.3 s (calibrated-style) to 2.2 s (shipped-style) warm, so 1,000 candidates cost 5-37 minutes. The table pays from about 10^4-10^5 candidates (joint search over 10+ weights and thresholds): numba re-scoring is 30-90x faster than a replay, numpy only 1-3x (about 2 s per candidate over a shipped-style 20.7M-row table, equal to the replay).

Decide what the table is for: (a) an execution-independent direction objective (forward mid move at 1-60 s and max up/down within 30/60 s, signed by the chosen side; metrics gross mid-to-mid edge and MFE-excess-over-no-skill) and (b) a cheap pre-screen; always confirm finalists in the full replay (0.3-2.2 s). Stops, trailing and order types stay out of the objective and are calibrated by hand.

Build it month by month with the engine's own decision branch (logging-only patch; trades and counters identical in all 18 month runs; scratch copy in events-baseline/xtools, built by make_patched.py): one row per C_DECISIONS evaluation at the lowest alert multiplier of interest (x7.5: 20.7M rows) or only x>=20 (about 2M rows); keep alert size in spreads as a column so thresholds re-apply offline; cost about 1.8 s per million rows and 2.3 GB peak per 4.3M-row month; add an episode id and weight by episode (1 to 151,484 rows per episode).

Store integer-valued features (points x2 as int16, spread as integer points) and reproduce the engine's tie rules (spread <= cap, body >= 21, micro > buffer): float32 storage made 0.03-3% of rows disagree, all at exact thresholds, and 6% of the calibrated preset's decision rows sit exactly at the 14-point cap. The replay's rebuilt quotes make those ties float-noise decisions; the live EA has its own noise from broker doubles.

The replay has no direction choice beyond with-the-burst or skip (winner equals burst direction in 100% of rows with a winner; against-burst trades come only from the EXHL fade). The order-flow simulator creates every other direction decision (up to +3.0 of votes, market route FOLM = 74% of real trades). Generate flow features per decision tick (23M shipped-style, 2M calibrated-style rows) or as per-tick float32 columns (250 MB per column for 62.7M ticks). The engine's npz store holds only t/bid/ask; the Hugging Face parquet (Nov 2025-May 2026) and the Dukascopy .bi5 files carry top-of-book bid/ask volume and would have to be re-extracted.

Validate any simulated flow label against the real account before using it: 2,584 real trades carry FA/FD/none labels (1,609/409/566), FD rates per route are FOLM:SM 139/965 = 14% and FOLM:BM 113/946 = 12%, the label did not predict outcomes (+5.7 pts, CI -5.4..+16.7), and 1,621 real entries lie inside downloaded ticks for a path check.

Plan statistics around episodes and folds, not trades: SE of the mean gross edge is 5.8 pts for 1,236 calibrated trades (SD about 200), a 10-pt difference needs about 6,300 trades per arm; the data hold 17.8k x30 and 127k x7.5 alert episodes (the episode count depends on the merge gap: 311k at 5 s, 127k at 20 s, 43k at 60 s at x7.5). Use the three splits as nested folds, keep the hold-out untouched during the search (the calibrated preset has already seen it) and correct for the number of candidates searched.

The bar to beat is concrete: shipped logic gross edge 0 (+0.7 +/- 1.2); calibrated entries +28.3 +/- 5.8 with total cost 18.5 vs the quote. A direction rule is better only if it raises gross edge (or MFE excess) on both buys and sells and in at least 4 of 9 months; sells (+17.7 vs +44.5 gross, 4 pts higher cost) and FLXQ:SS (about 0 outside the calibration months) are where the headroom is.

FlashGold-gate calibration is the slow axis: a native M5 series costs 0.14-0.31 s per month per distinct FG configuration (2.1 s for nine months) and about 5 s per replay in micro mode (project log: 97 replays in 489 s). Precompute the gate state per decision row for a grid of FG configurations instead of rebuilding per candidate. Evidence it matters: kept-by-gate trades +31.3 gross vs +7.0 for trades only taken without it (calibrated); no effect for the shipped preset.

Run settings for any new script: python -I -B, NUMBA_CACHE_DIR outside the repository (cold compile 34.3 s, cached load 0.15 s; the repository's tools/__pycache__ already holds a cache indexed at the current run_chunk line, I did not write to it), one month in memory at a time (0.6-1.0 GB), and the engine's cache keys: idx by lookback, candidates by (lookback, min points, multiplier), FilterSeries by FlashGold parameters.
